topology: tree3: core + two access switches, tables 3,500, idle 10 s, all monitored; one controller; 300 s, attack at 50 s; new-connection probe on
outcome: benign_harmed_pct from testbed/summarize_run.py (benign flow refused, blocked or evicted/deleted and back, at any switch on its path); eviction defenses: exact counts from the OpenFlow 1.4 monitor if T0 shows it works, else the poll inference
test: one-sided exact sign test on paired runs (same cell, same seed); a tie counts against the hypothesis; Holm within each hypothesis family; alpha 0.05

hypotheses.H1: T1, attacks A2, A4, E9P, 5 seeds: for each of SIFT, TableGuard, DMS-BTT, FTMaster, FTOP, rDefender, dualguard+portguard+hostid harms fewer benign flows over the 15 paired runs (Holm over the 6 baselines)
hypotheses.H2: T1, adaptive attack E9P: dualguard+portguard+hostid's mean harm over 5 seeds is below each of the 6 baselines' and below no defense's (descriptive, with seed ranges)
hypotheses.H3: T1, benign only, 5 seeds: dualguard+portguard+hostid's mean harm <= 0.5 % and mean lost first packets <= 1 %
hypotheses.H4: T1, A2, A4, E9P, 5 seeds: host identity (dualguard+portguard+hostid) harms fewer benign flows than port identity (dualguard+portguard) over the 15 paired runs
hypotheses.H5: T1-fed, domain D1, attacks A2 (seen only by another controller) and A6 (seen by none), 5 seeds: dualguard+portguard+hostid with federated models harms fewer benign flows than with local models over the 10 paired runs
hypotheses.H6: held out (never used in design): T4 attacks LA, HA, ALA, A2M (3 seeds) and T5 univ2 attacks A2, A4 (3 seeds): dualguard+portguard+hostid harms fewer benign flows than DMS-BTT (18 pairs), rDefender (18 pairs) and FTMaster (12 pairs, T4 only; no univ2 model), Holm over the 3

also_reported: the papers' columns per switch (avg/max attack share, table usage, earliest overflow, overflow seconds, Packet-In, Table-Full), lost first packets, probe success, flow-mods, controller and switch CPU, controller RSS; T2 (table 2K/4K) descriptive; ablation portguard+hostid descriptive
deviations: T5 uses SIFT in place of FTMaster: no univ2 FTMaster model, and training one needs simulator time during the campaign
each switch runs its own instance of every defense (the published defenses were described for one switch)
SIFT and TableGuard parameters selected by gate G1 on validation seeds (not stated by the comparison papers)
